title: "Python Code and Its Output, Together"
date: 2026-06-20
categories: [python, math]
description: "Write Python in a post; its results render inline at build time."
---

A code block runs when the site is built, and its output is baked into the page.
Readers see the source and the result side by side -- no server, no execution in
their browser.

## A computed value

```{python}
import numpy as np

x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 5)
np.round(np.sin(x), 4)
```

## A chart

The same setup produces a plot. The figure below is saved as a static image at
build time.

```{python}
#| label: fig-sine
#| fig-cap: "One period of the sine function."

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 200)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.2))
ax.plot(t, np.sin(t))
ax.set_xlabel("t")
ax.set_ylabel("sin(t)")
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```

Because results are pre-rendered, pages stay fast and the site remains fully
static.
